snippet.textDisplay:
RIGGED!! Like everything else in this country!! 
How the F is Alabama ranked 3rd in the country?! 
EXPLAIN THAT COMMITTEE!! 
Notre Dame beat the number 1 team in the country. They should be ahead of Alabama. Georgia beat Alabama. They should be in front of Alabama. Tennessee has the same number of losses as Alabama and they destroyed them. They should be in front of Alabama. Utah and UCLA are undefeated. They should be ahead of Alabama. Miami should have tied that game versus Notre Dame. They should be ahead of Alabama. Indiana has 1 loss by a foot and is the defending champion. They should be in front of Alabama 
Now lets put Alabama case. Who did they beat. 
Well they beat Kentucky. But how good really is Kentucky. Tennessee destroyed them. Kentucky best win is against LSU. But how good is LSU?! Another team Alabama beat. LSU did not beat Georgia, Tennessee, Texas or Mississippi. Again how good are they?! So those two victories versus these two teams and versus South Carolina who should not be ranked since Tennessee had 3 touchdowns taken away by a former Alabama player who was now the head ref. Suspicious you say?! They should be 5-4. 
This is the problem of the conflicts of interest that SEC has with ESPN/ABC who conduct these rankings with a obviously bias committee. Alabama has the biggest brand name in college the last 20 years, and want to get those TV Ratings. And the SEC gets such a bias look from this committee. 
You want to end this crap and fraudulent behavior?! 
PLAY EACH OTHER. 
Have a 13 game schedule with 8 conference games and 5 games versus other conferences. 
And only one game versus a team not from the 4 big Conferences. 
I want to see an Alabama team play in late November at Ohio St or Michigan. Or Georgia versus Indiana or Iowa in the cold. 
Lets also watch a Miami versus a UTAH also in November in  the cold. 
I see Texas plays Ohio St. I love it and respect them for it. 
In the past a Georgia team played a Clemson team. Also excellent. Wish the game was in late October or November instead of the first game. 
Every Year, I see an Alabama team play the same Auburn, Vanderbilt, South Carolina, Texas A&M. They do play LSU and Georgia. Miss St is the other team. 
Where is Texas, Florida and Mississippi?! Oklahoma beat them twice. We wont see that match up for awhile. 
And stop with these Alabama vs Mercer or LSU vs South East Louisiana games.
I have been watching college football since Steve Owens was playing for Oklahoma. That is a long time. You want to improve the game play each other.

Or rather the power 4 scheduling FCS and low tier G6 teams and they must play 10 qualifying opponents. Purdue, Arkansas, Vandy(?), Duke, Rutgers, Maryland, Colorado, Michigan State, etc would be considered the new "cupcake" games. Teams that are bad to Ok, aren't real threats in the playoff picture, but could still spoil a season if you sleep on them.

snippet.textDisplay: josh, you are mistaken about head to head MEANING A LOT.  just like most everyone else is.  it actually means very little.  lets sit back and take a look at what we are trying to do.  what is our goal ?  it is to pick teams, based upon how good they are.  just because team A beats team B, that does not mean that A is better than B.  how would they fare against dozens of other teams ?  i still maintain that the best way of judging a team is looking at who controls the game.  if i am betting my life, i will choose the 12 teams that are best at controlling the game.  because they are MORE LIKELY to win.  usc kills ohio state.  am i supposed to give them the same amount of credit as a team that played them earlier, when they had their qb, and were dominant ?  teams evolve on a weekly basis.  they have injuries, etc.  teams do not play with the same level of consistency.  you may beat a team on an off day.  some other team may face that same team, when it has an on day.  there are a lot of variables.  to really have an informed opinion, one needs to be watching all these games, where they can start to ask all these questions.  if they were truly doing that, there would not be nearly as many "surprises".  ucla is ranked 4th.  but did you know that of the 18 teams in the big 10, they have had the easiest schedule ?  they have a ranking of 72.  the second easiest one is penn state, at 57.  that is 15 points, a significant drop.  poor purdue is at 8, and oregon at 2.  which means that purdue has the 8th hardest schedule, and oregon the 2nd hardest schedule.

snippet.textDisplay:
The SEC dominates the top 25 because its schools have played the toughest schedules. The schedules are the toughest because the SEC's schools dominate the top 25. Chicken, egg.

The true genius of schedule strength is that it's a machine fueled by hyperbole and repetition, and it exists in a locker room where teams can neither enter nor exit. It is a room populated with the name brands, the ones we all accepted a decade ago were good because they had the pedigree, and no matter how much Wake Forest, Texas Tech or Boise State bang on the door, they'll never be let in.

Never mind that the ACC was 8-6 vs. the SEC last year. Never mind that the SEC hasn't had a team play for a national championship in the past three years. Never mind that Texas A&M and Oklahoma were top-10 teams to open the season but turned out to be pretty bad. (The same can be said for the Big10, where Penn State, Michigan, and Washington still manage to prop up teams' schedules long after being exposed as frauds.)

ACC has a bunch of 6-3 or better teams and only two ranked. The entire process is a charade. 24-teams just means more SEC (and maybe Big10) teams get into the invitational.

snippet.textDisplay: The Bama-Tennessee thing is easy to understand if you know how the committee works. Head-to-head matters, yes, but it’s not the only thing that matters. Bama has the #1 SoS and a higher SoR than Tennessee. Not to mention the committee knows the UGA game was stolen from Bama. It’s really not that complicated. You can disagree all you want, but the bottom line is too many people don’t understand how the system works. It’s about the entire season, not just one game.

snippet.textDisplay: CRAZY THOUGHT OF THE WEEK: After checking out the B1G tiebreaker for the Conference Championship game. Assuming that 1) USC wins out (beats Indiana and UCLA on the road and Maryland at home), 2) Indiana and UCLA win their other two games, and 3) Oregon, Ohio State, Wisconsin, and Iowa win out, there will be a six-way tie at 7-2 in conference between Indiana, Ohio State, USC, Oregon, Wisconsin, and Iowa. The first three steps in the B1G tiebreaker procedure all involve common opponents of all tied teams and there wouldn't be any. Step 4 is Strength of Conference Schedule, which would seem to favor USC in this scenario, since only USC will have played UCLA and four of the five other tied teams. If it does work out that way, USC would be playing UCLA twice in eight days. Even if they split those two games, it's still possible that both teams make the playoffs, and they could play a third time. Illinois could get into the mix, as well, but they would have to beat both UCLA and Iowa. And if both USC and Illinois beat UCLA, could it happen that only 1 team from the B1G, the 2-loss conference champion (could even be a 3-loss Oregon or Ohio State), makes the final bracket?
snippet.textOriginal: CRAZY THOUGHT OF THE WEEK: After checking out the B1G tiebreaker for the Conference Championship game. The first three steps in the B1G tiebreaker procedure all involve common opponents of all tied teams and there wouldn't be any. Step 4 is Strength of Conference Schedule, which would seem to favor USC in this scenario, since only USC will have played UCLA and four of the five other tied teams. snippet.textDisplay: At the end of the day, the playoff should be about identifying the best teams in the country and determining who has the ability to compete for and win a national championship. Strength of schedule absolutely matters, but it shouldn't be the only determining factor. We also have to consider overall performance, talent, coaching, quality wins, and the eye test. A team shouldn't automatically be penalized for a weaker schedule if it has consistently demonstrated that it can compete with the best. Likewise, a team shouldn't automatically be rewarded for playing a difficult schedule if it hasn't performed at the level expected. The real question should be: If these teams lined up against each other on a neutral field, who has the best chance of winning? Rankings should reflect the complete body of work while also recognizing which teams are genuinely capable of making a championship run. Ultimately, we're selecting playoff teams, not handing out awards for the toughest schedule.

snippet.textDisplay: @wallabygangsta That's exactly the problem with relying too heavily on statistics. Teams can rack up impressive points-per-game numbers against weaker competition, but that doesn't necessarily translate when they face elite defenses in the playoffs. A team averaging 45 points against inferior opponents might struggle to score 20 against a top-tier defense. Statistics need context. How a team performs against quality competition matters just as much as the numbers it puts up. Data should inform the rankings, not dictate them.

snippet.textDisplay:
​​​@ZeusssssssssOnly safe bet? Sure. But lol nobody outside Utah, Georgia, & UCLA are "safe bets" in literally ALL OF COLLEGE FOOTBALL atm. Aka, almost nobody is "safe" or "has a CFP lock" right now. But the Big XII is literally the only other conference along with the SEC with a realistic shot at getting >=3x teams into this thing. 🤷

And the chances of the Big XII getting at LEAST 2x teams in is near as close to a lock as is possible in this batshit crazy college football season. ALL THREE of the top Big XII teams behind Utah would need to take a loss for that to for sure not happen.

If either Texas Tech or BYU win out the regular season, they should make it in. (Especially if the other takes a loss, as it would open up another CFP spot without hurting either's resumes because they don't play each other).

And if on of the rare chance they BOTH take a loss somewhere during this final 3 week stretch, Houston is close enough at #14 to squeak into the CFP just as long as they manage to win out. (Especially if it's #25 Oklahoma State that takes down Texas Tech, whom Houston has a win over).

Aka, the top of the Big XII conference would basically need to completely IMPLODE over these final 3 weeks for the Big XII to only be a 1-bid league like most people expected it would be going into this season.
